Exercise B

Reading: Tips & Notices

Read the texts below, then answer the questions — just like Reading Parts 1 and 2 in the real MSA exam.

Part 1 — Match the Student to the Tip

Strong passwords: Use a long password with words, numbers and symbols, and never use the same one twice. If someone finds one password, they cannot open your other accounts.

Privacy settings: Check who can see your photos and posts. Set your profile to private so only friends can look at it.

Think before you post: Once a picture is online, you cannot take it back. Ask yourself: would I be happy if everyone saw this? Always ask before you post a photo of someone else.

Block and report: If a stranger sends you rude or strange messages, do not answer. Block the account, report it, and tell an adult you trust.

1 Jonas uses his football club name and 123 as the password for all of his accounts. He should read the tip about .

2 Priya has a public profile, so people she has never met can look at all her photos. She should read the tip about .

3 Tom put a funny picture of a classmate online without asking, and now the classmate is upset. He should read the tip about .

Part 2 — True or False?

Safe Surfing Club

The Safe Surfing Club meets every Tuesday at lunchtime from 1:00 to 1:30 in Room 12. Students from Years 8 to 10 are welcome, and the club is free. You do not need to sign up: just come along. Bring your phone or tablet if you have one. Each month the members make a poster with five new safety tips for the school corridor.

5 The club meets after school.

6 Members have to pay a small fee.

7 Students do not have to sign up.

Exercise C

Writing: A Forum Reply

Choose ONE of the two prompts below and write 120–150 words, just like Writing Part 3 in the real MSA exam. This section is graded by your teacher, not automatically.

Choose ONE prompt

Prompt 1 (forum post): “Our school wants to make an online safety lesson compulsory for every student. Some of my friends think it is a waste of time because they already know everything. What do you think?” Write a reply to this post. Say whether you agree and give reasons and examples.

Prompt 2 (forum post): “My parents want to check my phone and see who I write to. They say it keeps me safe. I think it is unfair.” Write a reply. Do you think parents should check their teenagers’ phones? Give reasons for your view.
